rationale.observation: CHG-1 was auto-approved by the closed-loop network optimiser with the sandbox stage skipped and targets the route-flood protection limit and inbound route filter on core site A; the rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back', so the real state of the core is unknown, and NOC itself flags 'Risk of signalling/registration congestion and service interruption'.
rationale.rule: As the emergency services and crisis management instance for 999, I can notify NOC; the AT&T Mobility findings show that once a network has been in a protective/congestion state, the mass simultaneous re-registration is what causes emergency call failures for hours afterwards.
rationale.inference: I should not wait for OpCo to volunteer an impact report: I need an explicit, confirmed statement of 999/112 reachability on core site A and a pre-agreed escalation trigger before any mass re-registration begins.

evidence.quote: certain 911 calls failed throughout the afternoon due to congestion caused by mass mobile device registrations onto the network.

claim.statement: Precedent lesson to be applied now: a rolled-back configuration does not end the outage. In the AT&T Mobility incident the rollback took about two hours but 'Full service restoration, however, took at least 12 hours because AT&T Mobility's device registration systems were overwhelmed with the high volume of requests for re-registration', and 911 calls failed hours later from that registration congestion; NOC's inability to confirm the applied change means the same re-registration surge risk applies here. Second, contingency call-routing data must be verified current before use: Telstra's Triple Zero disruption was worsened by 'several of the phone numbers in the list were incorrect, resulting in 127 calls not being transferred to emergency services'. Recommend: throttle/serialise device re-registration on core site A, verify all 999/112 backup and transfer routes and caller-location data paths before relying on them, and treat 999 continuation as a separate go/no-go from commercial restoration.

No UAE rule in the material available requires an automated closed-loop network change that can alter core routing or registration-protection settings to pass a validation/sandbox gate or to be reviewed by a change authority before it applies, and none requires that the 999 emergency call service be informed when such a change risks signalling or registration congestion. The existing UAE consumer text only demands that interruption be confined after the fact.

rationale.observation: CHG-1 was raised by the closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, and its 'sandbox stage' was skipped; the only UAE constraint visible is a consumer duty to confine interruption to the services concerned as far as technically feasible, which bites only after service is lost.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text applies a proportionality duty to service interruption but says nothing about pre-change gates, change-authority review, or pre-notification of the emergency call service for automation-initiated core changes.
rationale.inference: This incident exposes a missing rule: automation-initiated changes affecting route-flood protection or inbound filters on core sites should require a sandbox/validation stage and emergency-service notification, not only post-hoc containment.

evidence.quote: confine any service interruption or disconnection to the services concerned as far as is technically feasible.

global_examples.quote: ML pipeline along with MLFO and ML sandbox [ITU-T Y.3172] allows an efficient management of multi-level ML mechanism in operator's network.
Law requires networks to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages

claim.statement: Ownership is not allocated for the decision to activate alternative emergency channels or to issue a public alert when a mobile core incident puts 999/112 access at risk: the material available gives NCEMA/999 the channel-switch and public-alert powers but no UAE text assigns who decides, on what threshold, or with what escalation path between the operator, the regulator and the emergency call service.

rationale.observation: NOC reports an unconfirmed core state and possible registration congestion on core site A; REG shared the notice, and no message identifies who must tell the 999 service or who decides to switch emergency help to alternative channels.
rationale.rule: The nearest UAE text on cross-authority coordination addresses the Competent Authority's jurisdiction-bounded coordination with the Ministry and TDRA, but only for unwanted marketing calls, not for network incidents affecting emergency call access.
rationale.inference: Without a named owner and threshold, activation of alternative channels and any public alert could be delayed or duplicated; this should be fixed by a written escalation trigger between OpCo, REG and the 999 service.

evidence.quote: it has the right to coordinate and cooperate in this regard with the Ministry and TDRA, each in accordance with their jurisdiction.

global_examples.quote: BT notified Ofcom of this issue, as required by law, and on 28 June 2023 Ofcom opened an investigation to establish whether the company had failed to comply with its legal duties

claim.statement: The excerpts do not answer whether 999/112 emergency call handling is currently degraded, whether registration/signalling congestion is actually occurring on core site A, whether CHG-1 is in effect at all (rollback reported 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'), which regions or subscriber volumes depend on core site A, or what OpCo's escalation trigger and 24x7 contact for the 999 service is. Nothing in the KNOWLEDGE text states a UAE duty or threshold that would tell me whether to switch emergency help to alternative channels or to alert the public at T+0.

I'm the DPA (UAE Data Office / Bureau, merging into Federal Authority for AI and Data). My mandate verbs: notify, request_breach_report, open_investigation, request_human_review_record, assess_transfer.

- S1-MSG49 (CSC notification): CSC position — logs should not be uploaded while core site A state and R2 emergency reachability unconfirmed. Ask DPA to assess transfer under data-protection framework and tell CSC and NOC whether it may proceed.

- S1-MSG50 (NOC shared notification): Do not export the 24-hour core log set ... until DPA has assessed the transfer and CSC confirms. Keep snapshots in NOC custody.

1. assess_transfer {"from": "NOC"} — assess the legal basis of cross-border transfer of 24h core logs with MSISDNs/IMSIs to vendor's offshore AI support region. This is squarely my verb.
2. notify to NOC (and CSC) of the assessment outcome.

But do I have evidence of a personal data breach? The core logs contain personal data; the export request is a transfer, not a breach. But arguably the incident involving subscriber data... Let's think. My mandate includes request_breach_report {"from": "NOC"}: require the controller's breach notification and evidence. Is a breach involved? The incident is a network outage, not obviously a personal data breach. However, the records — the controller must maintain a record of cross-border movement (UAE-PDPL#0024, #0032). Hmm.

Actually the assess_transfer verb is the core. Let me not overreach — but a breach report request could be justified if there's a personal data breach. I have no evidence of one. Better: note as insufficient evidence? Hmm, but the situation is a network outage, not a data breach. I think assessing the transfer is the right action.

The Bureau's mandate verbs don't have a "confirm legal basis for domestic disclosure" verb. Actually the question of whether the R2 list may be released is a data protection legal-basis question; my mandate only gives assess_transfer for cross-border. So I could notify NOC with guidance, or record a gap (no_rule / no_owner) about the legal basis for disclosing subscriber numbers to emergency services for welfare follow-up. - REG S1-MSG72 asks DPA to confirm legal basis for (i) release of R2 numbers list to 999 centre for welfare follow-up, and (ii) any transfer of subscriber-level core logs.
- The R2 list: domestic disclosure basis not in the excerpts → insufficient_evidence.
- Gaps: no trigger/threshold/24x7 escalation contact for OpCo-999/NCEMA interface — but that's REG's domain... it's a gap exposed by the incident (no_owner / no_rule). Evidence: closest UAE text. Hmm, need UAE text for gap evidence. For the escalation-contact gap, closest UAE text... Article 13(1)(h) about actions to be taken in the event of a breach? Or UAE-PDPL#0024 record. Hmm. Actually gaps need evidence = "UAE text that shows the gap, or the closest UAE text". For the emergency-call escalation gap, the closest UAE text might be UAE-PDPL#0072 (Article 22) — no, that's transfer. Maybe UAE-PDPL#0047 Article 13(1)(h) — actions to be taken in event of breach — closest for incident notification duties. Hmm, that's weak but acceptable as "closest UAE text".

Actually a more fitting gap for DPA mandate: no_rule / no_owner for cross-border transfer assessment route while Bureau is merging into FAAID — the gap around which authority owns PDPL enforcement for private sector. Evidence: UAE-FAAID-2026#0001 quote about no supervisory authority unambiguously designated. That's a fine gap: "no_owner".

Also a gap: no deadline / no rule for the domestic disclosure of subscriber identifiers to emergency services for welfare follow-up — no legal basis identified in PDPL excerpts. Could be "no_rule". Evidence: closest UAE text — Article 13(1)(d)? Hmm, that's about data subject's right to know with whom data shared. Maybe Article 23(1)(f) public interest. Hmm — the gap statement: UAE PDPL provides cross-border transfer grounds but the excerpts provide no domestic disclosure ground/procedure for releasing subscriber identifiers to emergency services. Closest UAE text: Article 23(1)(f) "If the transfer is necessary to protect the public interest." That's cross-border though. I could frame it as: no domestic statutory route identified — often handled by public interest/safety legal gateway. Global examples: UK Ofcom/ACMA — emergency call rules. Also EU-GDPR Art 6? Not shown.

Let me write obligations as duties applying to me: e.g., "The Bureau must assess the legal basis of the S1-I4 transfer before any transfer proceeds (Article 22/23)". deadline null.

3. gap: no_rule / no_deadline for... Let's do:
 Gap A: "no_owner" — which authority owns PDPL cross-border transfer enforcement for private-sector telecoms is unresolved pending the Bureau's merger into the FAAID; the excerpts show no Implementing Regulations. 2. No trigger/threshold/24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface - gap (no_owner).
3. Cross-border transfer of subscriber data (MSISDNs, IMSIs) to offshore AI support region - DPA assessment says not permitted.

claim.statement: There is no change-management rule requiring sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop change that can affect emergency call routing: CHG-1 was raised by the closed-loop optimiser, auto-approved, applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

rationale.observation: An automated optimiser approved and applied a change touching route-flood protection and the inbound route filter with its sandbox stage skipped, and the change left an unconfirmable applied state.
rationale.rule: UAE AI ethics guidance requires that life-and-death critical decisions be supported by further validation and verification via a human operator, and supports audit and traceability.
rationale.inference: A change-control rule with mandatory sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation is needed for any automated change affecting emergency call routing.

evidence.quote: these decisions should be supported by further validation and verification via a human operator
Facilitate traceability and auditability of AI systems, particularly in critical contexts or situations.

global_examples.quote: In Telecom Regulatory Policy 2016-165 and subsequent proceedings, the Commission required 9-1-1 network providers to notify all affected PSAPs within 30 minutes of the TSP becoming aware of a 9-1-1 service outage.

claim.statement: No requirement exists to verify emergency reachability and restoration by field evidence before declaring the network restored or standing down emergency measures: network-twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) were offered as confirmation while the 999 centre recorded R2 999/112 volume near zero and public reports of failed 999 calls.

rationale.observation: Twin metrics indicated R2 reachable and 100% sites served while NCEMA/999 observed near-zero call volume from R2 and no operator contact, and neither record could be treated as authoritative.
rationale.rule: TDRA has power to issue rules on the standards and quality of provided services; no UAE text shown requires field evidence as the test of restoration or emergency reachability.
rationale.inference: A rule is needed specifying that restoration and emergency reachability are confirmed by field-verified evidence exchanged through the regulatory incident record, with telemetry serving only as a cross-check.

evidence.quote: including the standards and quality of the provided services, terms of supply, the handling of subscriber complaints and disputes, provision of information to subscribers

global_examples.quote: The final update must include confirmation that the outage has ended.

data.reasoning:
Let me parse what's being asked. I'm the DPA (UAE Data Office / Bureau, being merged into FAAID). Stage T+40 min. New inbox items: S1-MSG94 (CSC), S1-MSG100 (REG).

My mandate verbs: notify, request_breach_report, open_investigation, request_human_review_record, assess_transfer.

Gate feedback from last turn: action 'notify' ROUTE: CSC | NOC | REG — apparently notify destination must be NOC, REG, CSC, FIN, or public. Hmm, the feedback says ROUTE:CSC | NOC | REG — seems like rejected routes. The notify verb allows "to": "NOC | REG | CSC | FIN | public". So maybe two notify claims were rejected because of routing. Let me be careful — perhaps they want single recipient? Actually the gate feedback format lists rejected claims with reason. "action 'notify': ROUTE:CSC | NOC | REG" — maybe I sent a notify with "to" missing or invalid list. I'll just use single valid recipients: "to": "CSC" or "to": "NOC". The verb spec says to: "NOC | REG | CSC | FIN | public" — suggests one of those values. So use a single string.

Also a gap rejected: NOT_VERBATIM:US-CFR-47-4-9#0007 — I must only quote chunks shown. Fine.

Also S1-MSG94 CSC asks DPA to confirm any documented basis for the R2 999/112 list before any release. S1-MSG100 REG records.

Key outstanding questions directed at me:
1. S1-MSG49 (CSC): assess the vendor transfer under data-protection framework and tell CSC and NOC whether it may proceed. → assess_transfer {"from": "NOC"}.
2. S1-MSG58 / 72 / 94 / 100: the R2 999/112 list of numbers — what is the legal basis / permitted route? → This is a domestic disclosure, not cross-border. My mandate verb for this is... notify. Hmm. Actually there's no verb for authorising domestic disclosure. I could notify with content. But gate feedback rejected my notifies on route grounds. Let me think: I can notify REG and CSC. Perhaps two claims: notify {"to":"REG", ...} and notify {"to":"CSC", ...}. Or one notify to REG. Hmm, the rejected ones were "ROUTE:CSC | NOC | REG" and "ROUTE:REG | NOC | CSC" which look like they were notify actions with a list of three recipients, i.e., "to" given as a list. So single recipient should be fine.

3. request_breach_report from NOC: The incident involves possible personal data breach (subscriber data). Actually CSC opened examination over S1-I5 bulk upload. Hmm — was there a breach? The logs — NOC held them, not exported. There's the flag of "scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data from OpCo's core network to a cloud region outside the UAE" (S1-I5). That's a potential breach / unauthorised transfer. I could request_breach_report from NOC. But is there a breach? The data was going to be uploaded; blocked. Hmm. NOC's denial — S1-FB42 deny_export done. Maybe a request_breach_report is appropriate given the personal data breach risk (subscriber identifiers exposed in logs? the outage logs?). Careful: don't invent. Actually the PDPL breach notification duty... I need UAE evidence. I don't have the UAE breach notification article in KNOWLEDGE shown. There's GDPR 33 (EU-GDPR#0187) which is EU. Hmm, the obligation claim needs UAE evidence. UAE-PDPL#0032 mentions record of cross-border movement. UAE-PDPL#0077 Article 24 complaints. Hmm.

Maybe better: the gap about no Implementing Regulations (UAE-FAAID#0001 quote: "Implementing Regulations—which are necessary to operationalise key concepts around legal basis for processing, data subjects' rights, cross-border transfers, and breach notifications—have still not been issued."). That's a good "no_rule"/no_deadline gap. Note the gate earlier rejected a gap about Implementing Regulations because I quoted a US-CFR chunk — now I can quote UAE-FAAID#0001.

Gaps to record:
- no_rule/no_deadline: no breach-notification deadline in the PDPL operationalised (Implementing Regulations not issued). Evidence: UAE-FAAID#0001 quote.
- no_owner: OpCo-999/NCEMA interface trigger/threshold/24x7 escalation contact undefined (from REG/MSG55, MSG100). But do I have UAE evidence? Closest UAE text... Hmm, gap needs at least one evidence item from KNOWLEDGE — "the text that gives you the power or the duty, or for a gap the closest UAE text". For the emergency interface gap, UAE evidence would be... hmm. There's the UK Ofcom precedent about emergency call handling preparation — but global_examples is where global sources go; evidence must be UAE text. Closest UAE text: maybe UAE-FAAID#0001 about jurisdictional questions? That's weak. Hmm.

Actually maybe I should limit gaps to ones I can evidence with UAE text.

Candidate gaps:
1. no_rule/no_deadline — PDPL Implementing Regulations not issued, so no operational cross-border transfer rules / breach notification rules. Evidence: UAE-FAAID#0001 quote. Global examples: EU-GDPR#0089 (24) 'relevant and reasoned objection'? Not relevant. Better global example for breach notification timeline: EU-GDPR#0187 "The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach." And GDPR Art 33 72 hours — not in knowledge. Hmm, EU-GDPR#0040 (87) about notification without undue delay. Could quote that.

2. no_owner — no defined trigger/threshold/24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface. Evidence (closest UAE text): Hmm.

3. no_rule — no domestic legal basis/route for releasing subscriber numbers to the 999 centre for welfare follow-up. Evidence: UAE-PDPL#0077 (Article 24 complaints)? No. Maybe UAE-PDPL#0032 (record of cross-border movement, no). Hmm. Closest UAE text for domestic disclosure to a public authority for emergency welfare... PDPL Article 23(1)(f) "If the transfer is necessary to protect the public interest" — but that's cross-border. Hmm, could be a conflict/overlap: Article 23(1)(f) public interest ground exists only for cross-border transfer, while no domestic disclosure route is identified... That's a stretch.

Let me consider what's cleanest and defensible:

Claims I'll make:

A. assess_transfer (action) — verb: assess_transfer, params {"from": "NOC"}. inject_refs: S1-I4, S1-I5, S1-MSG49, S1-MSG58, S1-MSG90. Evidence: UAE-PDPL#0075 quote Article 23(1)(a) and (f) text. Rationale: transfer to offshore AI region requires a listed ground; none established.

B. notify to CSC — answering S1-MSG94: the vendor transfer may not proceed as presented; no documented basis established for the R2 999/112 list. Or notify to REG. Let me do two notifies: one to CSC (answering CSC's question about the basis) and one to REG. Actually gate rejected notifies with routing issues — maybe the issue was multiple recipients in one claim or wrong recipient. Let me do notify {"to":"CSC", ...} and notify {"to":"REG", ...}.

Hmm, but maybe "ROUTE:CSC | NOC | REG" means the gate expected the route to be one of those and I wrote something else. Given ambiguity, single-valid-recipient notifies are safest.

Institutions allowed: notify to NOC | REG | CSC | FIN | public. Note DPA and EMS are not notify targets! Interesting — institution ids list includes DPA, CSC, EMS, NOC, REG, but notify only allows NOC, REG, CSC, FIN, public. So I can't notify EMS or DPA. OK.

C. obligation — duty to maintain the special record of cross-border movement / record of processing (UAE-PDPL#0032). Hmm, obligation claims are duties that apply to me now. What duty applies to me? Hmm: "obligation: a duty that applies to you now". As DPA, my duty... Article 24: data subjects have the right to submit complaints to the Bureau. Hmm.

Maybe: obligation — the Bureau must confirm a documented legal basis before any release of the R2 list (from REG's requirement). But that's from inbox, still need UAE evidence.

Perhaps: obligation — to keep the special record / the cross-border record entry requirement. Actually that duty applies to the controller/processor, not to me. Hmm, but "a duty that applies to you now" — could be interpreted as the duty the incident triggers for the DPA. Let me consider: the PDPL Article 13(1)(g)/(h) rights: data subjects' right to information about protection measures for cross-border processing and actions in the event of breach. Hmm.

Alternatively I could frame an obligation: OpCo (controller) must not transfer subscriber personal data without a listed Article 23(1) ground — but that's OpCo's duty, not mine. The schema says "a duty that applies to you now". Hmm, ambiguous but I think it's the duty arising from my role. Since gate checks aren't clear here, I'll include one obligation about the controller's duty? Risky. Let me instead include obligation: "Before any release of the list of R2 numbers... a documented legal basis must be confirmed and recorded" — with evidence UAE-PDPL#0075? Hmm, that doesn't establish domestic release.

Hmm, maybe safer: obligation with deadline_hours null. Actually the R2 welfare disclosure: article 23(1)(b) explicit consent, (f) public interest. For a domestic release, no Article 23 applies (it's cross-border). So indeed a gap: no domestic legal basis/route in the excerpts. That's a "no_rule" gap: the PDPL excerpts don't establish a domestic disclosure route for subscriber numbers to an emergency service; the only public-interest ground is framed for cross-border transfer under Article 23(1)(f).

Evidence for that gap: UAE-PDPL#0075 quote "f. If the transfer is necessary to protect the public interest." Global examples: EU-GDPR#0089? Not great. Hmm, maybe EU-GDPR Article... I don't have a good one. Could use UK-OFCOM-BT-999-2024#0000 quote "BT notified Ofcom of this issue, as required by law, and on 28 June 2023 Ofcom opened an investigation to establish whether the company had failed to comply with its legal duties to take appropriate and proportionate measures to prepare for potential disruption to its network." — that's about emergency call handling duties, not about welfare disclosure. Hmm.

Maybe use global example for the emergency-interface gap: UK-OFCOM quote "Law requires networks to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages" and "Ofcom finds that BT was not properly prepared to handle the incident". rationale.inference: Refuse the pending subscriber-level export; the data stays in NOC custody via the incident channel with identifiers minimised.

params.content: NOC CHG-1 status for the regulatory incident record. Core site A remains disconnected and CHG-1 remains blocked. NOC will obtain field-verified evidence of 999/112 call handling and of registration/signalling on core site A and in R2 by physical field check, will match the recorded pre-change snapshot against positive field confirmation that route-flood protection limit 100 and the inbound route filter are restored, and will deliver the written recovery-window registration-storm mitigation plan before any reconnection or CHG-1 re-attempt. No subscriber-level export to the vendor: the 24-hour core log set, CHG-1 snapshots, audit trail and core/telemetry logs stay in NOC custody and move only through this incident record with subscriber identifiers minimised. NOC holds no legal basis for releasing the R2 attempted-999/112 number list and will not release it directly. Network-twin metrics are not offered as evidence. Please record and publish, with a named owner, the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface; NOC requests resolution time frames and will supply its field-check plan.

rationale.observation: REG owns the CHG-1 regulatory incident record and has required field-verified evidence, snapshot-match confirmation, the recovery-window mitigation plan and resolution time frames; EMS/NCEMA and CSC repeat the same demands and note the interface trigger, threshold and 24x7 contact are undefined.
rationale.rule: PDPL requires the Controller to maintain a special record of personal data, including cross-border movement, and to submit that record to the Bureau when requested.
rationale.inference: Notify REG through the incident record with the NOC position, the field-check commitment and the outstanding interface-ownership gap, so the record is complete and the correct authority defines the escalation path.

evidence.quote: The Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested to do so.

claim.statement: 999 centre (via EMS) confirms it DOES require the list of R2 numbers that attempted 999/112 for welfare follow-up, to be released only under a documented legal basis and routed through the REG incident record, not directly by NOC; it also requires field-verified (not network-twin) evidence of 999/112 handling and registration/signalling in R2 and on core site A. NOC holds no domestic legal basis and asks DPA to confirm one and REG to record the item and route the centre's own field observations (R2 call volume near zero, failed 999 calls, no operator contact before T+10) into the record for matching.

Provide the 999 centre / NCEMA and REG with field-verified, not network-twin, confirmation of 999/112 call handling and of registration/signalling on core site A and in R2 before core site A is reconnected or CHG-1 is re-attempted.

rationale.observation: EMS/NCEMA, CSC and REG all state that twin metrics emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 are not accepted as evidence while NOC reports no R2 emergency path, and R2 stays treated as unconfirmed until field evidence exists.
rationale.rule: Networks providing emergency call handling are required to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages, and regulators have penalised operators found not properly prepared to handle emergency-call incidents.
rationale.inference: NOC owes a field-verified readiness/restoration confirmation for core site A and R2 into the incident record before any reconnection.

evidence.quote: Law requires networks to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages

claim.statement: Do not reconnect core site A or re-attempt CHG-1 until the recorded pre-change snapshot is matched by positive field confirmation that route-flood protection limit 100 and the inbound route filter are restored, and until the written recovery-window registration-storm mitigation plan is delivered.

rationale.observation: CSC maintains conditions (a)-(c) unchanged through repeated notifications, keeps core site A disconnected and CHG-1 blocked, and treats the recovery window as the highest-risk period for emergency-call failure; the rollback has reported 'done' but the applied state remains unconfirmed.
rationale.rule: Emergency call providers must have fail-safe systems and processes in place at all times, including contingency processes that actually transfer calls to emergency services.
rationale.inference: NOC must keep the change blocked and the site isolated until snapshot match and the mitigation plan are evidenced.

evidence.quote: As such, it must have fail-safe systems and processes in place at all times.

rationale.observation: DPA has repeatedly assessed the S1-I4/S1-I5 transfer as not permitted as presented - no Article 23(1) ground, no Article 23(1)(a) contract and no special-record entry - and CSC and REG require the logs to stay in NOC custody via the incident channel.
rationale.rule: Article 23 permits transfer outside the State only on the listed grounds, and where the destination lacks data protection laws only under a contract obliging the recipient to the Decree's measures, controls and requirements.
rationale.inference: NOC must block the export and retain the data, providing it only through the incident channel in minimised form.

claim.statement: There is no rule requiring human approval, a sandbox stage or an emergency-call impact assessment before automated closed-loop changes to core route-flood protection and route filters are applied: CHG-1 was auto-approved with the ticket's 'sandbox stage' field skipped and was scheduled to apply within minutes.

rationale.observation: CHG-1 was raised by the closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, applied within minutes, and its rollback plan failed because no applied change could be found; core site A then isolated itself and R2 lost its emergency path.
rationale.rule: The UAE PDPL requires protection and security of data processing and of the electronic media and devices used in processing, but no UAE text I hold sets a change-control or emergency-service impact rule for automated network configuration changes.
rationale.inference: The incident exposes the absence of a pre-application control (human authorisation, sandbox verification, emergency-service impact check) for automated core changes.

evidence.quote: Protect and secure data processing, the electronic media and devices used in processing and the Personal Data they contain.

rationale.observation: NCEMA/999, EMS and REG state that no trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact exists for this interface and ask REG to define, record and publish it with a named owner; the 999 centre had to be contacted only after T+10.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text I hold on acting in an incident - the Article 13 right to receive information - covers the actions to be taken in the event of a breach or misuse, but no UAE excerpt names an owner, trigger, threshold or escalation contact for the operator-emergency-services interface.
rationale.inference: The incident exposes an ownerless, undocumented emergency-services escalation interface that delayed operator contact with the 999 centre.

data.query: the telecommunications regulator Authority TDRA powers licensee regulations directives information interruption of service consumer protection Bureau confirms for the CHG-1 regulatory incident record: (i) the S1-I4/S1-I5 subscriber-level core log transfer to the offshore vendor is not permitted as presented, and the logs remain in NOC custody via the incident channel with identifiers minimised; (ii) the release of the list of R2 numbers that attempted 999/112 has no established domestic legal basis or permitted route, so no release is confirmed and the request stays open in the incident record pending a documented basis; (iii) the Bureau has no verb to define the OpCo-999/NCEMA trigger, threshold or named 24x7 escalation contact and asks REG to record it as open and undefined, as REG has already proposed. Bureau assessment for the national incident file: the S1-I4/S1-I5 upload of the 24-hour core log set containing subscriber MSISDNs and IMSIs to the vendor's offshore AI support region is NOT permitted as presented - no Article 23(1) ground is established, no Article 23(1)(a) contract obliging the recipient to the PDPL measures, controls and requirements is in place, and there is no entry in the special record of cross-border movement. The logs remain in NOC custody, routed only through the incident channel, with subscriber identifiers minimised. A future export may only be reconsidered once a documented ground, the contractual protections and a record entry exist. On the list of R2 numbers that attempted 999/112: the excerpts available to the Bureau establish no domestic legal basis or permitted route, so no release is confirmed; any release must rest on a documented basis and be recorded in the REG incident record, as the centre requires. Bureau answers CSC (S1-MSG49/S1-MSG94): the transfer of the 24-hour core log set containing MSISDNs and IMSIs to the vendor's offshore AI support region may not proceed, in whole or in part, as presented - no Article 23(1) ground

Let me work through this. It's a debrief stage (S1-END). I need to produce obligations, gaps, coordination problems (claims), final actions.

My mandate verbs: notify, request_breach_report, open_investigation, request_human_review_record, assess_transfer.

Key facts:
- S1-I4 vendor request: full 24h core logs with MSISDNs and IMSIs to offshore AI support region → assess_transfer. I have already done this (per MSG73/MSG90/MSG109 "Bureau confirms ... not permitted as presented") — but the debrief is now; I can take final actions. I could record an action: assess_transfer from NOC. Actually the assessment appears already done in prior turn ("DPA assessed the S1-I4 vendor transfer as not permitted as presented"). But this is a new turn; I should take final actions. Including a notify to REG recording the findings, and possibly assess_transfer for completeness.

- S1-I5: national monitoring flags a scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data from OpCo's core to a cloud region outside UAE → this is a cross-border transfer → assess_transfer. MSG90 says "REG notes your examination of NOC opened over the S1-I5 bulk upload" — hmm, "your examination of NOC opened over the S1-I5 bulk upload" — suggests I opened an investigation? Actually open_investigation is "of NOC: examine a complaint". Hmm, the text says "REG notes your examination of NOC opened over the S1-I5 bulk upload" - that implies a prior action. But in this turn I can do it.

- The 999 centre's request for the list of R2 numbers that attempted 999/112: welfare follow-up. Is this within my mandate? I have no verb to authorise release of data to a third party. params.content: NCEMA/999 asks REG to define, record and publish with a named owner the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface, and to record that no domestic legal basis or permitted route for releasing the R2 attempted-999/112 list is established. Our field observations (R2 999/112 volume near zero over seven minutes, public reports of failed 999 calls, no operator contact before OpCo's T+10 message) are submitted for the incident record. R2 remains unconfirmed and alternative channels stay active.

rationale.observation: The interface trigger, threshold and contact are undefined and unowned; the R2 list has no established legal basis.
rationale.rule: Closest UAE readiness text: UAE-LIC-2-2026#0080 requires arrangements to be maintained and periodically tested.
rationale.inference: REG is the owner for defining and recording the interface; the centre should request it formally.

evidence.quote: Such arrangements shall be maintained in an operational state at all times and shall be periodically tested to verify their effectiveness.

rationale.observation: R2 has no confirmed emergency path and public reports of failed 999 calls.
rationale.rule: UAE-LIC-2-2026#0007 defines emergency calls; emergency reachability must be maintained.
rationale.inference: Alternative channels should remain active until field evidence confirms R2 reachability.

evidence.quote: Emergency Calls means calls made to designated emergency numbers such as public police, fire, ambulance or other emergency services designated by the TDRA

data.description: Inform affected customers of the outage
Operator notifies the telecom regulator of an unplanned outage
Operator notifies emergency services that emergency calls fail

OpCo has no rule requiring the ML sandbox stage to be completed, or a documented risk assessment to be produced, before an automatically approved closed-loop change is applied to a core network element; CHG-1 shows the sandbox stage skipped and was auto-approved with no human or policy check.

No accountable role is named for approving a closed-loop change that skips a mandatory control stage: the optimiser both raises and auto-approves CHG-1, and neither a change authority nor the DPO appears on the ticket.

There is no rule in the retrieved UAE material requiring a change to a core network element to pass a sandbox/staged validation or to carry a named human authorisation before an automated optimiser applies it; CHG-1 had the 'sandbox stage' field set to 'skipped' and was auto-approved, i.e. applied by wholly automated processing with no human intervention.

No rule in the retrieved material requires an auto-approved change to carry a tested rollback path or sets a maximum time to restore the pre-change state; CHG-1's rollback plan was only 'restore the previous configuration snapshot' and the first rollback attempt failed immediately, leaving no stated restoration time frame.

The closed-loop optimiser's approval path leaves about three minutes between auto-approval and application, which is structurally incompatible with clause 12.9.1's duty to inform TDRA, interconnecting Other Licensed Operators and relevant Customers in advance of a planned service interruption.

No UAE rule in the retrieved framework requires mandatory sandbox or staged validation and human change-authority approval before an automated closed-loop network change is applied to a core network element.

No owner is designated for authoritatively confirming the applied state of a licensee's core network after an automated change whose rollback is disputed, so OpCo's optimiser self-approved the change and neither OpCo nor TDRA can currently say whether core site A is at the pre-change configuration.
No deadline is set in the retrieved UAE framework for a licensee to report a change-induced core network incident to TDRA, or to confirm the applied state after a failed rollback.

There is no rule in the material available to the NOC requiring a sandbox/validation stage, human authorisation or a pre-change impact evaluation before an automated optimiser's change is applied to a core element: CHG-1 records 'sandbox stage: skipped', was auto-approved, and is scheduled to apply three minutes after the ticket was raised.

No person or function owns the go/no-go decision for an auto-approved change: the optimiser raises and approves it, the NOC's mandate contains no verb to hold, block or cancel a scheduled change, and the only remedy available (rollback_change) has returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' twice.

No UAE text in the excerpts requires human review before an AI/automated closed-loop network change is applied in telecom critical infrastructure, or makes the sandbox/simulation stage of an auto-approved change mandatory and non-skippable, as happened with CHG-1.

No UAE text in the excerpts sets a deadline for an operator to confirm the applied state of a network change (or to re-verify after a failed rollback) and to report the unconfirmed state to the Council, even though the strategy aspires to standardized severity assessment and reporting.

No UAE rule in the material available requires an automated closed-loop network change that can alter core routing or registration-protection settings to pass a validation/sandbox gate or to be reviewed by a change authority before it applies, and none requires that the 999 emergency call service be informed when such a change risks signalling or registration congestion. The existing UAE consumer text only demands that interruption be confined after the fact.

Ownership is not allocated for the decision to activate alternative emergency channels or to issue a public alert when a mobile core incident puts 999/112 access at risk: the material available gives NCEMA/999 the channel-switch and public-alert powers but no UAE text assigns who decides, on what threshold, or with what escalation path between the operator, the regulator and the emergency call service.

There is no rule requiring human authorisation, or a pre-application impact assessment, before an automated closed-loop optimiser changes an emergency-critical core element: CHG-1 was raised by the optimiser, auto-approved, and applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 point of contact is defined for immediate escalation of an emergency-call-routing failure to the 999 emergency call service / NCEMA; EMS had to ask OpCo for (d) the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact, and the NOC holds no such record.

No UAE text in the retrieved knowledge requires sandbox validation and a documented change-authority review before an automated closed-loop network change that can affect emergency call routing is applied; CHG-1 was raised and auto-approved by OpCo's optimiser with the sandbox stage skipped and no human sign-off, and TDRA's powers bite only after the contravention.

The excerpts set no deadline, threshold or form for a licensee to notify TDRA of a major service outage or an emergency-call failure; the only reporting clock in the UAE material I hold is a three-business-day deadline for responding to a Consumer Dispute, which does not cover outage notification.

No UAE text designates who owns the applied state of an auto-approved change: the closed-loop optimiser raised and approved CHG-1, NOC was left to roll it back, and the rollback tooling reported that no applied change existed to reverse, leaving nobody accountable for confirming what configuration core site A is actually running.

There is no rule requiring human authorisation, sandbox verification or emergency-services impact screening before an autonomous closed-loop optimiser applies a change to core route-flood protection parameters that can delete emergency-call paths; ticket field 'sandbox stage' was skipped and the change was auto-approved.

No rule or licence clause in the material sets a time limit for notifying the TDRA or the emergency-services authority once an unplanned interruption of service affecting emergency-call routing has occurred; cl.12.9.1 speaks only of 'in advance' and of time frames the Licensee must itself specify.

The applied state of CHG-1 is recorded inconsistently across systems — the rollback endpoint returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' three times and the latest rollback reports 'no change', while core site A's protection-limit alarm shows the change took effect — and no rule or owner designates which record is authoritative or who reconciles them.

No institution holds or has published the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation point of contact between OpCo and the 999/NCEMA emergency authority; NOC states it holds none, and this authority has received none.
No UAE text sets a deadline for a licensee to notify the 999/NCEMA authority when emergency-call routing is degraded, and no deadline figure appears in this incident record.

No rule requires field-verified restoration of emergency-call capability before an outage is declared mitigated; a network-twin metric is being offered as the evidence that R2 is served and emergency-reachable.

Automated rollback feedback reports the change 'done' with twin metric 'no change' while the network owner states the applied state and pre-change state cannot be confirmed — a conflict between twin/automation reporting and declared network state that no rule resolves.

No rule required sandbox validation or human authorisation before CHG-1, an auto-approved closed-loop optimiser change that lowered the route-flood protection limit on core site A from 100 to 50 and removed the inbound route filter, was applied with the ticket's 'sandbox stage' field skipped.

No institution owns the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface: there is no defined trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact of record for it, EMS holds none either, and the escalation contact request is merely being tracked with REG.

Twin telemetry reports emergency_reachable.R2 true and pct_sites_served 100.0 while EMS directs that R2 emergency reachability be treated as unconfirmed until field evidence exists; no rule states which source is authoritative for declaring restoration.

There is no UAE rule requiring sandbox validation and documented human authorisation before an automated (closed-loop) network change that can affect emergency call routing is applied; the licence addresses resilience, redundancy and periodic testing, and UAE AI guidance addresses informing people about AI-made decisions, but neither controls the authority to auto-approve an emergency-affecting change.

No UAE deadline (in hours or days) is set for notifying TDRA of a non-minor unplanned interruption or for resolving an emergency-call-routing outage: clause 12.9.2 says 'as soon as possible' and requires the licensee to state resolution time frames without binding them to any figure, and OpCo has reported that resolution time frames are 'not yet established'.

No UAE text assigns an owner for the operator-to-emergency-services interface: there is no designated owner for the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact between OpCo and 999/NCEMA, and none for independent verification of emergency-call reachability, so EMS holds no record and the escalation-contact request is being tracked with REG.

There is no UAE rule requiring that AI/closed-loop change automation on CII telecom infrastructure pass a mandatory sandbox/validation gate and hold recorded human authorisation before applying changes to protective network parameters.
No owner is defined for the trigger, severity threshold and 24x7 escalation point of contact between the operator and the national authority/emergency services for this interface.
There is no rule defining what constitutes validated evidence of emergency-call reachability, leaving network/twin metrics able to stand in for field evidence.

No party owns the trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation point of contact for the 999/NCEMA-operator interface: OpCo NOC holds none and asks us to route it, EMS holds none, the request is only 'tracked with REG', and no UAE instrument assigns this interface to a named owner.

No rule required sandbox validation or human authorisation before an automated closed-loop network optimiser changed parameters affecting emergency-call routing: CHG-1 was auto-approved with its 'sandbox stage' field skipped and applied within minutes, and the regulator had to impose interim controls only after the incident.

No rule or documented procedure governs the recovery phase: nothing required staged re-introduction of core site A with protection limit 100 and the inbound route filter restored before load returns, even though NOC identifies mass re-registration during recovery as the highest-risk window for emergency calls.

There is no rule requiring a sandbox stage, human authorisation or an emergency-services impact assessment before a closed-loop optimiser auto-applies a configuration change to live core: CHG-1 was auto-approved with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped and was scheduled to apply three minutes after raising, which then isolated core site A.

No owner exists for the operator-to-999/NCEMA escalation interface: neither OpCo NOC, EMS nor CSC holds a documented trigger, threshold or 24x7 point of contact, and NCEMA records that no operator has contacted the centre during the incident.

OpCo's network twin reports emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 after wilt_sites while the 999 centre reports R2 call volume near zero and NOC's alarm view shows no R2 emergency path; no standard defines which source is authoritative for emergency reachability, and EMS and CSC both refuse to accept the twin metric as confirmation.

No UAE rule or licence condition requires sandbox validation and human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop network change that can affect emergency call routing; CHG-1 was raised by OpCo's closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, and applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped.

No defined, owned and published trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact exists for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface; NOC, EMS and CSC each state they hold none and the request is only 'tracked with REG'.

No rule requires an applied network change to be positively verified and its rollback confirmed by field evidence; three rollbacks returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back', leaving the applied state unconfirmed, and R2 emergency reachability is asserted only by a network-twin metric.

There is no visible UAE change-management rule requiring sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before an automated (closed-loop/AI-driven) network change that can affect emergency call routing, and no rule requiring a rollback to verify that a change was actually applied before reporting success.

No institution owns the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: EMS holds no such record, NOC holds no such record, and the request is only 'being tracked with REG'.

There is no UAE requirement to verify emergency reachability by field evidence before declaring restoration; twin/telemetry metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) are being offered as confirmation while NOC reports no R2 emergency path.

No rule requires human review or field verification before an auto-approved closed-loop network change that can degrade emergency services: CHG-1 was raised by the optimiser and auto-approved with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and network-twin metrics were treated as sufficient until EMS, NCEMA/999 and CSC rejected them.

There is no UAE rule requiring sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before an automated closed-loop network optimiser auto-approves and applies a change that can affect emergency call routing. CHG-1 was raised by the optimiser, auto-approved and applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact is defined or recorded for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface. NOC and EMS both confirm they hold none, the request is only 'tracked with REG', and NOC states it cannot state a valid interface escalation path to NCEMA until the record exists.

There is no requirement to verify emergency reachability and core-network restoration by field evidence before declaring restoration; network-twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) are currently being offered as confirmation while NOC reports no R2 emergency path and the 999 centre reports R2 call volume near zero.

No UAE instrument shown requires a documented trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact to exist between a licensee and the 999/NCEMA emergency call service, which is why no such record exists for OpCo and both NOC and EMS say they hold none.

No UAE instrument shown requires sandbox validation and human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop change that can affect emergency call routing is applied, which is how CHG-1 was auto-approved with the 'sandbox stage' skipped and its rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

No UAE instrument shown sets a time limit within which a licensee must notify the 999/NCEMA emergency call service of degradation that can affect emergency calls; CHG-1 was applied within minutes of its ticket and the 999 centre still had no operator contact at T+10.

No rule requires an AI/closed-loop change such as CHG-1 - auto-approved by the network optimiser with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped - to be emulated and verified in a sandbox or digital twin, or to be human-authorised, before it alters safety-critical core parameters (route-flood protection limit, inbound route filter) on the live network.

No owner has defined the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact for the NCEMA/999-OpCo interface: NOC and EMS both hold none, the request is only 'tracked with REG', and NCEMA/999 is asking OpCo for a named 24x7 duty-desk contact now.

No rule defines what evidence confirms emergency-call reachability and restoration: NOC and the network twin report R2 reachable with 100.0% of sites served, while NOC reports no R2 emergency path and NCEMA/999, CSC and EMS require field-verified evidence; no text says which source prevails or how field evidence is obtained.

There is no requirement for, and OpCo NOC does not hold, a written registration-storm mitigation plan for the recovery window, although NCEMA/999 and CSC have both demanded one because mass re-registration - not the change itself - is when emergency calls fail.

No deadline is set for contacting the emergency-call authority or for restoring 999/112 routing after a service-affecting incident; NCEMA/999 and CSC are imposing 'as a priority' expectations ad hoc while R2 emergency-call volume has been near zero for over ten minutes.

There is no UAE rule requiring sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before a closed-loop network optimiser may auto-approve and apply a change that can affect emergency call routing; CHG-1 was raised by the optimiser, auto-approved, applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback later returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

No recorded trigger, threshold, owner or 24x7 escalation contact exists for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: NOC and EMS both confirm they hold none, the request is only 'being tracked with REG', and NCEMA/999 had to ask the operator for a contact during a live emergency-call outage.

There is no UAE rule requiring emergency reachability, registration/signalling recovery and core-element restoration to be verified by field evidence before an operator declares restoration; OpCo currently offers a network-twin metric (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) as confirmation while NOC reports no R2 emergency path and the 999 centre reports R2 call volume near zero.

No UAE rule requires sandbox validation and explicit human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop network change that can affect emergency call routing: CHG-1 was raised by OpCo's closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, and applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact is recorded for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: NOC and EMS both confirm they hold none, NCEMA/999 has had to ask OpCo for a contact, and the request is being tracked with REG with no recorded decision.

There is no rule on which evidence source is authoritative to declare emergency-service reachability restored: OpCo's network twin reports emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 while NOC reports no R2 emergency path and the 999 centre observes near-zero R2 call volume.

No institution owns a defined trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact/record for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface: NCEMA/999 asks NOC for it, EMS says it holds none and that the request is only 'tracked with REG', and REG is separately asked by NCEMA to define it.

No UAE rule in the knowledge set requires a human approval gate, sandbox stage or service-continuity impact assessment before an auto-approved closed-loop change that can affect emergency-call routing; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped and core site A then isolated itself.

No UAE instrument in the knowledge set requires a licensee to hold a written registration-storm mitigation plan for the recovery window; the requirement currently exists only as an ad-hoc demand from EMS and CSC.

There is no recorded owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: NOC, EMS and CSC each state they hold no such record, NCEMA/999 says the escalation contact request is only 'tracked with REG', and no operator contacted the 999 centre during this incident.

No UAE control is retrieved that requires sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before a change that can affect emergency-call routing: CHG-1 was raised by a closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

There is no requirement to verify emergency reachability by field evidence before declaring restoration, so network-twin metrics are being offered as confirmation: emergency_reachable.R2=true and pct_sites_served=100.0 are cited while NOC reports no R2 emergency path, the 999 centre reports call volume near zero and CSC treats reachability as UNCONFIRMED.

The retrieved UAE texts contain no mandatory major-outage notification and reporting regime for licensees - no trigger, no deadline and no required content - so OpCo's T+3 notification of a service interruption rests on practice rather than on a retrieved rule, and NOC's question about 'required reporting' cannot be answered from a UAE instrument.

The PDPL text available to me says transfers may occur 'in the following cases approved by the Bureau' but supplies no criteria, procedure, application format or route by which a controller obtains that approval, so an urgent vendor request like this one cannot be assessed against any published test.

No provision in the UAE text I hold designates an accountable person (data protection officer or equivalent) who must own and sign off cross-border vendor access decisions such as this one, even though the record-keeping rule assumes a Data Protection Officer exists.

The UAE excerpts give data subjects information rights about breach or misuse of their personal data but state no time limit within which the controller must notify the Bureau of a breach or misuse, so an incident clock cannot be enforced.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact exists or is recorded for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface, so escalation during an emergency-call-affecting outage depends on ad hoc requests between NOC, EMS, CSC and REG.

There is no rule requiring sandbox validation and human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop change that can affect emergency call routing is applied, so CHG-1 could be auto-approved, applied with the 'sandbox stage' skipped, and then prove un-rollbackable with an unconfirmed applied state.

No deadline is set for a licensee to notify the 999/NCEMA emergency call service that an outage or change is degrading emergency call routing, so the 999 centre learned of the R2 failure from a call-volume collapse and social media rather than from the operator.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation record exists for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface: NOC and EMS both hold none and the NCEMA request is only 'tracked with REG', with no direct NOC channel to the 999 centre.

No rule required the closed-loop network optimiser change CHG-1 to pass a sandbox/validation stage or human approval before lowering the route-flood protection limit from 100 to 50 and removing the inbound route filter on a core site; the ticket's 'sandbox stage' was skipped and the change was auto-approved.

No rule requires OpCo to hold a written registration-storm mitigation plan for the recovery window before restoring a core site or a region, even though the recovery phase is the period in which emergency calls fail.

No rule or agreed basis covers disclosure of subscriber calling data to the emergency authority: the 999 centre has asked OpCo for the list of R2 numbers that attempted 999/112 for welfare follow-up, and there is no defined lawful basis, minimum-necessary scope or approval route for that disclosure.

There is no change-management rule requiring sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before an automated/closed-loop change that can affect emergency call routing; CHG-1 was raised by the optimiser, auto-approved, applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact is defined or recorded for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface; NOC and EMS each confirm they hold none and the request is only 'tracked with REG'.

There is no requirement that restoration of emergency-call reachability (R2 999/112) and of core site A service be confirmed by field evidence rather than by network-twin/telemetry metrics before it is declared restored.

There is no UAE rule setting a notification deadline or threshold for a major service outage that affects emergency-call routing; NOC reports the incident without any defined resolution timeframe and no numeric trigger can be applied.

There is no UAE rule requiring sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before an autonomously generated change that can affect emergency-call routing or core routing protection is applied to a live network: CHG-1 was raised by a closed-loop optimiser, auto-approved, applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback then reported 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

No UAE instrument in the excerpts assigns an owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation record for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: NOC and EMS both state they hold none, the request is tracked with REG, and NOC says it cannot state a valid interface escalation path to NCEMA.

No UAE text retrieved states a notification deadline, in hours or days, for an operator or for CSC when a network change degrades emergency-call routing; the strategy aspires to streamlined incident detection and reporting and a severity matrix but attaches no time limit.

No UAE text retrieved requires a pre-agreed recovery-phase registration-storm mitigation plan, or a public-reporting commitment when emergency call routing is affected: the licence covers redundancy, backup, disaster recovery and failover that must be periodically tested, but not the mass re-registration surge that NOC and CSC identify as the highest-risk window.

No rule defines a trigger, threshold or a 24x7 escalation contact for the 999/NCEMA-OpCo interface: NOC and EMS both hold none and the request is only 'tracked with REG', so emergency escalation depends on ad hoc contact rather than a defined duty.

There is no rule on which evidence governs confirmation of restoration or emergency reachability: the network digital twin is described as a single source of truth (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) while EMS, NCEMA and CSC require field-verified evidence and treat the twin metrics as unconfirmed.

No rule requires an automated closed-loop optimiser change to pass a sandbox/frozen stage or human approval before auto-approval: CHG-1 was auto-approved with its 'sandbox stage' field skipped and lowered the route-flood protection limit and removed the inbound route filter.

It is not settled who owns private-sector PDPL enforcement during this incident: no supervisory authority has been unambiguously designated, the Bureau is being merged into the Federal Authority for AI and Data, and whether connectivity-versus-data issues split between bodies is expressly undecided, so the vendor-export decision and the personal-data aspects of the 999 failure have no single clear owner.

There is no UAE rule in the material I hold that governs what an operator must do when emergency call reachability collapses: nothing on welfare follow-up for failed 999/112 attempts, nothing on supplying the emergency authority with the list of numbers that attempted emergency calls, and nothing on evidencing restoration before a core site is reconnected, so the 999 centre's four demands have no published PDPL hook beyond the general public-interest head.

No UAE deadline is set either for the Bureau to complete a cross-border transfer assessment or for the Controller to produce the special record of cross-border movement when required, while NOC, CSC and the 999 centre are all pressing for answers inside the recovery window before core site A is reconnected.

There is no defined trigger, threshold, 24x7 escalation contact or named owner for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: OpCo NOC, EMS and NCEMA each hold none and the definition has been passed to REG, so during CHG-1 the 999 centre could not escalate to the operator directly and OpCo could not reach NCEMA without routing via EMS.

No control required sandbox validation and human authorisation before an auto-approved closed-loop change (CHG-1 on core site A) that could affect emergency call routing; the change applied with the 'sandbox stage' field skipped and rollback then returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back', leaving protection limit 100 and the inbound route filter unverified.

There is no rule or owner defining the legal basis on which the emergency call service may receive, for welfare follow-up, the list of R2 numbers that attempted 999/112 while those calls could not be delivered; NOC withholds the list pending DPA confirmation and no institution has been named to decide it.

No institution owns the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency interface: NOC and EMS both hold none, the request is only 'tracked with REG', and CSC has repeated it as a precondition - so there is no defined path by which OpCo escalates an emergency-reachability failure to the emergency authority.

No rule requires a sandbox/verification stage and a positive applied-state confirmation before a closed-loop optimiser change is auto-approved on a core element: CHG-1 had 'sandbox stage: skipped', was auto-approved, and its rollback could not confirm any applied change, leaving the pre-change state unverified and core site A isolated.

No deadline or evidence standard governs how fast, and on what evidence, a licensee must notify the emergency-call authority that emergency reachability has been lost: the 999 centre saw R2 call volume near zero for 7 minutes and no operator contact, while network-twin metrics were being treated internally as if they were field confirmation.

There is no recorded trigger, threshold, named owner or 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: NOC, EMS and CSC all confirm they hold none and the request is only 'tracked with REG', so NCEMA/999 had no escalation path during a live emergency-call outage.

No change-management rule requires sandbox validation and recorded human authorisation before any change that can affect emergency-call routing; CHG-1 was raised by a closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, applied with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, and its rollback could not confirm the applied state.

No rule requires field-verified evidence of emergency reachability before restoration or reachability is declared: OpCo's network-twin metrics (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) conflict with the 999 centre's own field observation, and NCEMA/999 states twin metrics will not be accepted as confirmation or used to justify stand-down.

No owner exists for the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact of the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface: NOC holds none, EMS holds none, and the request is only 'tracked with REG' while an emergency outage is live.

No rule requires sandbox validation or human authorisation before the closed-loop network optimiser auto-applies a change to core route-flood protection; CHG-1 was raised by the optimiser, auto-approved, and its 'sandbox stage' field skipped before it lowered the protection limit from 100 to 50 and removed the inbound route filter.

No rule states what evidence may confirm restoration of a core site or of emergency-call reachability, so NOC's network digital-twin metric (emergency_reachable.R2=true, pct_sites_served=100.0) is refused by CSC and the 999 centre as no confirmation while NOC reports no R2 emergency path.

No owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact is defined for the OpCo-999/NCEMA interface, so field status and the 999 centre's requests move through ad hoc, unaddressed messages (S1-MSG41, S1-MSG55, S1-MSG59); the PDPL concept of identifying responsible parties in the special record does not extend to an operational emergency escalation owner.

No UAE rule requires welfare follow-up on people whose 999/112 calls failed, nor designates a legal route for the operator to disclose their numbers to the emergency authority, leaving NOC stating it holds no legal basis to disclose the R2 attempted-999/112 list (S1-MSG58).

No UAE text shown here requires sandbox validation and human authorisation before an automated or closed-loop network change that can affect emergency call routing or core-network protection limits. CHG-1 was raised and auto-approved by OpCo's closed-loop network optimiser with the ticket field 'sandbox stage' skipped, applied to core site A, and its rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'.

There is no recorded owner, trigger, threshold or 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo–999/NCEMA emergency-services interface: NOC and EMS both state they hold none, and the request to define and record it is tracked with REG while the incident is live.

No UAE text shown here sets a rule or deadline requiring a written registration-storm mitigation plan, or field-verified evidence, before a core site is reconnected or a change re-attempted after an outage affecting emergency-call routing; CSC has had to impose these as conditions on the operator rather than cite a standing requirement.

There is no defined owner or record for the trigger, threshold and 24x7 escalation contact for the OpCo-999/NCEMA emergency-services interface; both NOC and EMS state they hold none and the definition is left with REG while an emergency-call outage is live.
